doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Oberlin jazz club and Dave Brubeck in the Jazz Nativity
summary: She helped form a jazz club that brought in Dave Brubeck, and later used his song in the Jazz Nativity.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: formed the first jazz club because there was no jazz out there. In fact the conservatory wouldn’t let us use the conservatory piano for the concert when we brought Dave Brubeck in.
And that’s when I met Dave and fortunately we had been in touch because I used one of his songs in the jazz nativity and he was in it and his son Chris was a king.
Oh. Chris was a king. Was it “God’s Love Made Visible” that you used?

I heard that in the “Fiesta de la Posada” when it was first done up in Connecticut before it had its real performance. And I just loved it. And so years later when I was writing the “Jazz Nativity” I realized that after the manger scene, what a perfect thing. So I called him and he said yes.
